{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ks-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c09671c50f252a5c2fe6dfe97d3a1e49ea06af883cc6fa5f92858e707c44c162","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ks-class-c:lineage:32","source_registry_sha256":"c7fb2073a9e8bb6a73d0151458fe04991b703d84f882b00a01bedfcea433c383","source_liveness_sha256":"94328be42cc10cf86af8e486b41bc40c72c45e4700d27b9b46d1f3d2feac7bb6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Safe driving","heading":"C2 — Safe driving","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Safe driving

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A64
When tailgated and an empty lane is available, move into it to let the other vehicle pass. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A64
If tailgated without an empty lane, wait for a clear road ahead and then slow gradually to encourage a pass. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A64
Do not brake sharply to discourage a tailgater; it raises rear-end and aggressive-driving risks. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A64
The handbook recommends adding two to three seconds to the front following interval when being followed too closely. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A64
Avoid staying beside another vehicle on a multilane road; adjust speed to preserve lateral room. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A64
On a two-way road, avoid crowding the centerline; the lane center generally leaves room to evade either way. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A64
Make room for merging traffic by moving to the next lane when that lane is clear. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A64
Leave extra room beside parked cars without crossing the centerline because doors, people or vehicles may enter the path. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A64
Give pedestrians and cyclists, particularly children, additional space for unexpected movement. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A64
When a tractor-trailer passes, moving toward the outside of the lane can increase separation while remaining within the lane. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A64
Select a merge gap that leaves time to establish a suitable following interval rather than forcing into a small opening. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A64
Cross multiple lanes one at a time because checking several at once is difficult and can create conflicts. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A65
After stopping before crossing traffic, allow enough gap to get fully across; the handbook's normal-condition example is about three to five seconds. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A65
When entering traffic with a turn, allow room both to complete the turn and to accelerate. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A65
The handbook's normal-condition right-turn-and-acceleration example takes about 12 to 15 seconds. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A65
Its normal-condition left-turn-and-acceleration example takes about 15 to 18 seconds. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A65
Do not begin crossing even on green if vehicles block the exit path. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A65
Before a left turn, confirm that neither vehicles nor pedestrians will trap the vehicle in the opposing path. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A65
Do not enter merely because another driver's turn signal is on; wait for the turn to begin and a genuinely safe gap. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A65
Another vehicle's signal may indicate a later turn or may have been left on accidentally, especially if it does not self-cancel. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A65
Cross railroad tracks only when there is room to clear without stopping on them. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A65
Complete a pass as promptly as safety permits to limit time beside another vehicle. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R23 | anchor: A65
Before passing, check oncoming traffic, side-road entries and slowing vehicles ahead, as well as mirrors and the rear blind spot. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R24 | anchor: A65
Signal a safe pass and begin from at least two seconds behind the vehicle being overtaken. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R25 | anchor: A65
Steer smoothly into the passing lane, keep checking ahead and in mirrors, and avoid drifting toward the passed vehicle. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R26 | anchor: A65
Before returning after a pass, see the entire front of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror, then signal and return smoothly. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R27 | anchor: A66
When being passed, move toward the right side of the lane and maintain a steady speed. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R28 | anchor: A66
Passing permission from signs or markings still requires enough safe space. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R29 | anchor: A66
The handbook recommends passing one vehicle at a time and warns that a pass can take as long as 20 to 30 seconds. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R30 | anchor: A66
Do not attempt a pass when an oncoming vehicle is visible; if time or distance is uncertain, wait. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R31 | anchor: A66
Oncoming vehicles can appear slower than their actual closing speed, making passing-distance judgment difficult. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R32 | anchor: A66
The handbook's perception warning says a vehicle more than 25 seconds away may look stationary; visible closing motion may mean less than 25 seconds remains. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R33 | anchor: A66
For passing near hills or curves at 55 to 60 mph, the handbook calls for at least one-third mile of forward view, about 20 to 25 seconds. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R34 | anchor: A66
Treat a hill or curve that blocks the view as hiding opposing traffic and do not start passing within one-third mile of it. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R35 | anchor: A66
Do not pass in intersections, and avoid passing at other crossing points such as driveways, alleys or parking entrances. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R36 | anchor: A66
Before a pass, look for pedestrians, cyclists, narrow bridges, ice, potholes or obstructions that may force another vehicle sideways. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R37 | anchor: A66
Do not pass without room to return to the travel lane, and do not depend on other drivers creating that room. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R38 | anchor: A66
The handbook advises against passing with a railroad crossing in the next 20 to 25 seconds of travel. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R39 | anchor: A67
Allow extra space for drivers whose view is blocked at intersections or driveways and for drivers backing into the road. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R40 | anchor: A67
Give extra room to people whose vision is obstructed by icy windows, umbrellas or lowered hats. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R41 | anchor: A67
Use additional caution or space around distracted people such as delivery workers, construction workers and inattentive pedestrians. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R42 | anchor: A67
Allow for confused drivers who slow unexpectedly or search for directions or addresses. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R43 | anchor: A67
If a passing driver runs short of space, slow down to help that vehicle return safely. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R44 | anchor: A67
If another driver needs an abrupt lane change, slowing to let that driver merge can reduce conflict. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

Misconceptions: Mirrors leave blind spots; a green signal does not prove a clear path; ABS does not promise a shorter dry-road stop; another driver's signal does not guarantee a turn.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: search, assess, choose, act. The cue summarizes the decision sequence without adding a rule.
Glossary: Visual lead, perception distance, reaction distance, braking distance, hydroplaning, ABS, ESP and space cushion are defined in the sourced blocks.
Dynamic facts: Numeric examples are bound to this edition and their stated conditions; legal requirements, equipment behavior and unresolved timing ranges need issuer or vehicle-manual rechecking.

FACT_ID: sec07-R45 | anchor: A67
Handle hazards separately when possible; delay passing a roadside pedestrian until an opposing vehicle has gone by. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R46 | anchor: A67
Communicating location and intended movement helps other road users anticipate the vehicle's actions. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R47 | anchor: A67
Use headlights to improve the vehicle's visibility to others, especially when rain, snow or fog reduces visibility. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R48 | anchor: A67
The handbook states that Kansas requires headlights whenever the vehicle's wipers are used. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R49 | anchor: A68
Switch on headlights as daylight fades; doing so slightly early helps other drivers see the vehicle. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R50 | anchor: A68
Use headlights while driving away from a low rising or setting sun to help opposing drivers see the vehicle. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R51 | anchor: A68
Keep headlights clean and working and have a qualified person check their aim to preserve visibility without dazzling others. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R52 | anchor: A68
A horn can warn of an imminent collision, including a pedestrian entering the street or vehicles about to strike one another. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R53 | anchor: A68
Do not use the horn to greet someone, complain about an error or pressure a driver to move faster. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R54 | anchor: A68
Avoid sounding the horn near a blind pedestrian. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R55 | anchor: A68
If possible during a breakdown, notify authorities by phone or another device; roadside signs may give an emergency number. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R56 | anchor: A68
For a breakdown stop, move away from traffic and off the road when possible. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R57 | anchor: A68
Turn on hazard flashers to indicate a disabled vehicle. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R58 | anchor: A68
Choose a breakdown stopping place visible to approaching users rather than just beyond a hillcrest or bend. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec07-R59 | anchor: A69
The handbook describes placing warning flares about 200 to 300 feet behind a disabled vehicle to alert approaching drivers. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec07-R60 | anchor: A69
Do not remain in the roadway or attempt a tire change within a traffic lane. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec07-R61 | anchor: A69
A white cloth on the antenna, mirror or door handle, or a raised hood, can indicate a disabled vehicle. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec07-R62 | anchor: A69
Signal changes in direction or slowing so other road users can anticipate the movement. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec07-R63 | anchor: A69
Use turn signals before intersection turns and the lane-change signal function for lane changes or merges. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec07-R64 | anchor: A70
After a turn or lane change, check that the signal has canceled and switch it off if necessary. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R65 | anchor: A70
Brake lights communicate slowing; reduce speed as early as safely possible. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R66 | anchor: A70
When slowing unexpectedly, the handbook recommends three or four light brake-pedal taps to warn following traffic. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R67 | anchor: A70
Warn before slowing to turn off a road without a separate exit or turn lane. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R68 | anchor: A70
Warn before parking or turning before an intersection when followers may expect continued travel through it. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R69 | anchor: A70
Warn before slowing for a hidden hazard or traffic queue that a close follower cannot see. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R70 | anchor: A70
A driver's license is a privilege rather than a right. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R71 | anchor: A70
Drive without drug, alcohol or other impairment. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R72 | anchor: A70
The driver and passengers should always wear seat belts. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R73 | anchor: A70
A minor and the minor's parent or guardian bear financial consequences of the minor's driving. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R74 | anchor: A70
Drivers are responsible for parking without obstructing traffic or pedestrians and preventing the vehicle from rolling away. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R75 | anchor: A70
Courtesy helps address situations that traffic rules do not explicitly cover. [A70]
Source: [A70 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec07-R76 | anchor: A71
Assess personal driving limitations, vehicle limitations and road or weather conditions as sources of risk. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R77 | anchor: A71
Large vehicles may be less stable with restricted surrounding visibility, while small vehicles may be harder for others to see. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R78 | anchor: A71
Manage identified risks through position and speed changes; risks can be reduced but not completely eliminated. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R79 | anchor: A71
Position or speed changes can increase response time, improve control and separate conflicting hazards. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R80 | anchor: A71
Driving decisions improve with practice and experience. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R81 | anchor: A71
Begin decisions with an active search for other users, their positions and their paths. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R82 | anchor: A71
After identifying road users, assess their movement and whether they could collide with the vehicle. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R83 | anchor: A71
Responses can include changes in speed, changes in direction and communication; take action after choosing the response. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R84 | anchor: A71
Practice anticipating a possible hazard, deciding how to reduce its risk and then acting. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0071]
